caption_draft: UGO-Omics platform architecture and underground-organ atlas. The figure summarizes the biological scope and data structure of UGO-Omics, including a broad 51-species underground-organ atlas, an 11-species high-confidence analytical backbone, organ-category annotations, orthogroup-based candidate transfer, and researcher-facing discovery tools. This tiered design separates atlas breadth from analytical depth and provides the foundation for cross-species underground-organ candidate discovery.

Integrated evolutionary framework of UGO-Omics. The 51-species atlas provides broad taxonomic and underground-organ coverage, while the 11-species high-confidence backbone supports phylogenetic and module-level analysis. The BUSCO-based species tree was reconstructed from the main 9-of-11 BUSCO matrix, and candidate modules were overlaid as species-level recurrence signals. Underground-organ categories are shown as species-associated annotations. The figure provides phylogenetic context for interpreting candidate module recurrence and is not intended as a definitive reconstruction of underground-organ origins.

Researcher-facing UGO discovery workflows. UGO-Omics supports multiple entry points for underground-organ research, including protein sequence queries, gene-list queries, species-based resource exploration, organ-focused kits, demo outputs, and use-case guidance. These workflows convert UGO-Omics from a static data collection into a reusable discovery platform for candidate prioritization and cross-species comparison.

Regeneration-resilience toolkit model for underground-organ diversification. Morphologically distinct underground organs may arise from different developmental contexts, but they share functional demands for persistence, regrowth, developmental-state switching, regulatory control, and structural remodeling. UGO-Omics identifies candidate signals consistent with recurrent modular reactivation of a conserved regeneration-resilience toolkit. This model is hypothesis-generating and does not imply strict organ homology or functional validation of individual genes.

Known-category recovery and high-impact biological discovery case. UGO-Omics recovers expected biological categories related to meristem/bud regrowth, stress survival, hormone-mediated developmental switching, transcriptional regulation, structural remodeling, and organ identity or patterning. Integrating recurrence, benchmark recovery, phylogenetic dispersion, and species-level support identifies a recurrent regeneration-resilience core toolkit, with cell-wall remodeling as a supporting structural component. The analysis supports candidate prioritization and future testing.
